unsupported_codes.reason: Blindness and low vision: reporting a code from this category, legal blindness included, makes a diagnosis from the acuity that the technician recorded. The provider documents neither blindness nor low vision.

citations.H35.3134: ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY2027, Section I.A.19: the assignment of a diagnosis code is based on the provider's diagnostic statement that the condition exists. Section I.B.14: code assignment is based on the documentation by the patient's provider; the listed exceptions, for which another clinician's documentation may be used, do not include visual acuity. Section I.C.7.b: when 'blindness' or 'low vision' of both eyes is documented without the visual impairment category, H54.3 is assigned. Here the ophthalmologist's diagnosis is nonexudative age-related macular degeneration of both eyes, advanced atrophic with subfoveal involvement, which the bilateral code with that stage reports in full; the best corrected acuity of 20/200 in each eye is in the technician's entry, and the ophthalmologist documents neither blindness nor low vision, so no code from category H54 is reported.

coder_notes: The table at category H54 places a best corrected acuity of 20/200 in visual impairment category 1, which is why a code from H54 is tempting. The table grades an impairment that the provider has documented; it does not replace that documentation. The geographic atrophy and the tomography findings are part of the diagnosis. One code covers both eyes. In practice this documentation would lead to a provider query; the gold is what can be reported from the note as written.
